I235.screening_reason: Personalized learning platform; well-being is a marginal component
I235.summary_en: Proposes CourseSphere AI, a conceptual LLM-based platform for personalized learning, query resolution and assignment support, including an emotional support module for stress. No data or empirical results are reported.

I236.summary_en: Analyzes usage of a digital employee well-being platform with k-means clustering and descriptive analytics. Three user groups are identified: short-term (95.5%), intermediate (3.4%) and long-term users (1.1%).

I237.best_result: Random Forest (FCP) accuracy 100%, F1 100%; OR accuracy 98.29%
I237.summary_en: Develops a web application with Random Forest models to detect social media addiction risk in adolescents in real time, using over 10,000 records (ARS questionnaire and usage monitoring) and a sample of 120 school students. Models reach 93.93% to 100% accuracy depending on the addiction dimension.

I238.screening_reason: Mixed population (school pupils, college students and professionals); unclear abstract
I238.summary_en: Proposes deep belief networks to predict mental health disorders from survey responses labeled with unsupervised learning, targeting high school pupils, college students and professionals. No sample size or metrics are reported.

I239.screening_reason: Not about mental health; studies preferred place of study
I239.summary_en: Compares several algorithms on questionnaire responses from 400 students about studying at home versus in hostels. Logistic Regression yields the highest accuracy and students prefer studying at home.

I240.screening_reason: Mixed population (students and employees); no data or results
I240.summary_en: Proposes using machine learning to predict stress levels in college students and employees. No data, algorithms or results are described.

I241.summary_en: Scoping review of multimodal AI for early detection of mental health conditions in UK university students, covering ten primary studies (from logistic regression and SVM to LightGBM, XGBoost and cross-modal transformers). Multimodal integration consistently outperforms unimodal approaches, although interpretability, dataset diversity, validation and ethics remain challenges.

I242.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical fitness test software
I242.summary_en: Proposes Android software for college physical fitness testing and compares test data by grade and year. Reported results are incoherent with the stated aim.

I243.summary_en: Proposes an AI platform that analyzes speech, facial expressions and text messages with machine learning, NLP and emotion recognition to detect student stress in real time and offer chatbot support. No data or results are reported.

I244.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical fitness
I244.summary_en: Applies multiple machine learning models to identify factors influencing college students' physical fitness scores. No data or results are described.

I245.summary_en: Presents the NikoMood application, which collects daily mood and activity data and uses Learning Vector Quantization to identify students at risk of academic stress, with linear regression to forecast the number at risk. The forecast achieves a MAPE of 22.93%.

I246.summary_en: Examines the relationship between physical exercise, anxiety and resilience in 1,700 college students from Fujian using PARS-3, SAS and CD-RISC, k-means clustering and mediation analysis. Exercise negatively predicts anxiety and resilience plays a partial mediating role.

I247.summary_en: Studies the effect of academic demands on depressive symptoms using 1,303 questionnaires from high school students, Random Forest and PCA. Academic stress, test scores and family support show significant relationships with depressive symptoms.

I248.summary_en: Presents MindEcho, a stress perception and early warning system for college students based on multi-source text mining and a BiLSTM-Attention fusion model, deployed as a mini-program with graded intervention. The model achieves the best recall on high-risk samples; the dataset is not described.

I249.summary_en: Proposes a logistic regression model trained on homomorphically encrypted data (TenSEAL) to predict student mental health while preserving privacy. The encrypted model reaches 84% accuracy versus 96% unencrypted, with scalable resource consumption.

I250.summary_en: Analyzes seven years of Twitter posts on mental health with topic modeling and sentiment analysis. Sentiment is positive overall but has declined since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

I251.best_result: Logistic Regression accuracy 84%, ROC-AUC 0.908; Decision Tree 65.3% (severity)
I251.summary_en: Proposes a two-step explainable screening of mental health risk using a survey of 500 Sri Lankan university students (DASS-21 and lifestyle variables): logistic regression for risk and a decision tree for severity. Logistic regression reaches 84% accuracy (AUC 0.908), and SHAP highlights help-seeking, meal regularity, socialization and sleep duration.

I252.screening_reason: Not about mental health and no data analytics
I252.summary_en: Proposes pathways for universities to promote online and ideological-political education through new media matrices. No data analytics is applied.

I253.summary_en: Applies k-means clustering to medical student data (age, health status and self-reported stress) to identify profiles. Three clusters with different combinations of health and stress levels are found.

I254.summary_en: Compares BERT, RoBERTa and LoRA-fine-tuned Gemma-3-4B-it for classifying student mental health conditions in a dataset of 9,823 text samples across seven categories. RoBERTa slightly outperforms BERT, and Gemma does not improve performance despite higher computational cost.

I255.summary_en: Proposes using machine learning and eye-tracking to improve mental health support for engineering students. No data, method details or results are reported.

I256.summary_en: Predicts student depression from a dataset of student records with 17 demographic, academic and lifestyle features using six algorithms. AdaBoost performs best (accuracy 84.80%), and sleep duration, academic pressure and family history of mental illness are the strongest predictors.

I257.screening_reason: Not about mental health; self-regulated learning
I257.summary_en: Proposes an early recognition system based on predictive analytics, sensors and wearables to support self-regulated learning in Higher Education 4.0. No data or results are reported.

I258.summary_en: Classifies nomophobia severity in university students using 113 survey responses and LLMs fine-tuned with QLoRA (Qwen 3, Mistral 7B, Gemma 2B, Phi-3 Mini). Qwen 3 achieves the best performance (accuracy 92.25%).

I259.screening_reason: Outcome is engagement with a digital intervention, not mental health
I259.summary_en: Presents EngageTriBoost, a stacked ensemble (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) predicting engagement of 1,673 at-risk college students with a digital mental health intervention from 108 baseline features. It reaches up to 84% accuracy, and SHAP links engagement with chronic pain, stigma and alcohol use.

I260.summary_en: Proposes a mental well-being chatbot for students using NLP and sentiment analysis, with crisis alerts and Spotify-based music recommendations. No data or metrics are reported.

I261.summary_en: Combines fuzzy logic and decision trees to classify faculty well-being in higher education using a synthetic dataset of 1,000 samples. The hybrid model reaches 96.8% accuracy, outperforming logistic regression and SVM.

I262.summary_en: Uses the Empatica EmbracePlus wearable and deep reinforcement learning to study the relationships between emotional intelligence, stress and physiological signals in master's students at Texas A&M University. No sample size or results are reported.

I263.best_result: Psychological recovery rate +7.3%; platform usage rate 97.2%
I263.summary_en: Develops a cloud-based college psychological counseling platform that uses k-means clustering to group students by type of psychological problem. It reports a 7.3% increase in psychological recovery rate, without describing the data.

I264.summary_en: Assesses mental health from a large dataset of demographic, lifestyle and social behavior variables using Boosting, Decision Tree and Logistic Regression. Boosting achieves the highest accuracy (81.75%).

I265.summary_en: Develops an intervention chatbot for university students trained on 424 question-answer records derived from the DASS-21, comparing Random Forest and Multinomial Naive Bayes. Random Forest reaches 82.5% accuracy versus about 66% for Naive Bayes.

I266.summary_en: Clusters university student profiles with unsupervised learning using wearable and questionnaire data (parental education, income, academic and physical activity) and relates them to PHQ-9 scores through feature importance and ANOVA. Walking activity and exercise patterns are the main drivers of depression-related clusters.

I267.screening_reason: No data analytics; mental health education course
I267.summary_en: Describes introducing computer information technology into a group-counseling mental health education curriculum. No data, analytic method or measurable results are presented.

I268.screening_reason: Not about mental health and no data analytics; physical education intervention
I268.summary_en: Evaluates the effect of a sports program on the physical fitness of 155 fourth-grade students in Beijing. Lung capacity and several fitness tests improve significantly, but BMI does not.

I269.summary_en: Predicts stress in 215 first-semester Israeli university students from psychometric assessments (distress, self-esteem, positive traits) using an AOA-CNN-XGBoost model. It reaches a mean accuracy of 89.27%, outperforming CNN and AOA.

I270.summary_en: Proposes an ensemble (KNN, Naive Bayes, XGBoost) to predict the happiness index of school children from socio-demographic, academic, psychological and physiological features. No sample size or metrics are reported.

I271.screening_reason: General health risk, not specifically mental health
I271.summary_en: Presents BeHealthy, a blockchain-powered AI system that predicts health risks in students from personal and lifestyle data. No data, model details or results are reported.

I272.summary_en: Compares Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, SVM and Naive Bayes to detect stress, anxiety and depression in higher education students. Decision Tree is best for stress (94.4%), SVM for depression (91.2%) and Logistic Regression for anxiety (88.76%); the data are not described.

I273.summary_en: Predicts student stress with several algorithms (Logistic Regression, XGBoost, KNN, Random Forest, Voting, Gaussian Naive Bayes) within an MLOps pipeline. Gaussian Naive Bayes reaches 89.1% accuracy; the data are not described.

I274.summary_en: Predicts student mental health during COVID-19 using a Kaggle survey dataset, five classifiers and XAI techniques (LIME, SHAP). No metrics are reported.

I275.screening_reason: Does not address students; conceptual text without data
I275.summary_en: Discusses the use of big data and artificial intelligence for depression screening and early warning. No data, method or results are presented.

I276.screening_reason: Not about mental health; estimates sexual orientation
I276.best_result: 24-split Random Forest (highest accuracy, F1 and AUC)
I276.summary_en: Estimates the share of sexual minorities among Beijing college students using the BCSPS panel survey and Random Forest with repeated random sub-sampling. The estimate is 5.71%, almost twice the self-reported 3.03%.

I277.summary_en: Presents a multimodal system combining facial emotion recognition, wearable sensor data and NLP of reflective text to detect stress, anxiety and academic burnout in university students. Multimodal analysis is reported to outperform single-source methods on real and synthetic data, without metrics.

I278.summary_en: Analyzes with statistical and machine learning tools the relationship between caffeine consumption and the physical and mental well-being of healthcare students in the UAE using a structured questionnaire. No sample size or results are reported.

I279.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical health
I279.summary_en: Applies k-means clustering to seven physical health test indicators of college students. Female students show better overall physical quality, and both sexes need to improve lower-limb strength and endurance.

I280.summary_en: Classifies anxiety using a Kaggle survey dataset of 1,997 university students in Bangladesh, selecting 18 of 39 features and comparing six algorithms with SHAP. Linear SVM achieves 92.68% accuracy.

I281.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical health
I281.summary_en: Develops an intelligent physical health assessment system for college students using IoT sensors, Random Forest and KNN on records of over 2,000 students. It reports 99% accuracy.

I282.summary_en: Develops a mental health crisis early warning system from surveys of 1,500 undergraduates at three Chinese universities (PHQ-9, GAD-7, employment anxiety, social media use) using Random Forest with SMOTE. It reaches AUC 0.903; employment anxiety is the second most important predictor, and SHAP and partial dependence plots provide interpretability.

I283.summary_en: Develops a visual analytics dashboard to explore the psychosocial effects of COVID-19 on university students, comparing pre- and during-pandemic data across four dimensions. The psychological impact is more negative during the pandemic.

I284.screening_reason: Outcome is comprehensive student evaluation; mental health is only an input variable
I284.summary_en: Proposes a Random Forest model for comprehensive student evaluation integrating academic performance, extracurricular activities, mental health and social abilities, using 3,500 students and 42 features. It reaches 87.3% accuracy.

I285.summary_en: Examines psychological resilience as a mediator of academic achievement in engineering and MBA students from Nagpur, using a psychometric resilience instrument administered at two time points. A predictive framework is proposed, but the analytic method and metrics are not described.

I286.summary_en: Presents a multimodal AI mental health companion that detects emotional states from text (NLP), voice and facial expressions and provides self-care advice. No data or results are reported.

I287.summary_en: Proposes an ensemble (KNN, Naive Bayes, XGBoost) to predict the happiness index of school-age children from socio-demographic, academic, psychological and physiological features, with recommendation reports for low scores. No sample size or metrics are reported.

I288.summary_en: Analyzes factors associated with poor mental health using a Google Form survey of people from various professions, including students, with Power BI and machine learning classification. Algorithms and results are not reported.

I289.summary_en: Investigates stress management among undergraduate students using surveys and machine learning to identify contributing factors and stress stages, informing a chatbot intervention. Algorithms, sample size and results are not reported.

I290.summary_en: Predicts university students' stress levels with several classifiers using a Kaggle dataset of 1,100 instances and 19 attributes on academic, social and lifestyle factors. Random Forest achieves 97.45% accuracy.

I291.summary_en: Presents an explainable machine learning framework for detecting student depression from behavioral, academic and demographic data, using LIME and ELI5 for interpretability. It reports 98.41% accuracy without specifying the algorithms or dataset size.

I292.summary_en: Develops an AI screening tool using Random Forest on a synthetic dataset of 1,000 students with passive digital behavior features (sleep patterns, screen time, sentiment of online communications). It identifies high-risk students with 87.3% accuracy; screen use during sleep and negative sentiment are the strongest predictors.

I293.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep quality, not directly mental health
I293.summary_en: Builds an SVM model to identify factors of sleep quality using 583 questionnaires from first- and second-year students at Xi'an Eurasia College. The model reaches 96.26% prediction accuracy.

I294.summary_en: Applies decision tree and random forest models to college students' psychological data and designs a driving game with classical music and natural scenery to relieve stress. Game effectiveness is reported as verified experimentally, without data or metrics.

I295.screening_reason: Population not specifically students (digital platform users)
I295.summary_en: Proposes a system using machine learning and NLP to analyze linguistic patterns, sentiment and behavioral indicators in digital platform interactions to detect depressive tendencies. No data or results are reported.

I296.summary_en: Evaluates a smart planning course to help adolescents manage digital device use through a quasi-experiment and a multimodal learning analytics approach. The intervention shows few significant effects, while the analytics approach provides richer data than traditional methods.

I297.summary_en: Predicts mental health outcomes in 314 Bangladeshi university students from 26 universities using a 66-question survey, feature selection (PCA, RFE-RF) and six models. Decision Tree reaches the highest accuracy (98.41%).

I298.best_result: LSTM (better accuracy and response time than RNN)
I298.summary_en: Develops a college mental health monitoring system based on sentiment analysis of students' posts on campus social platforms using sentiment dictionaries and LSTM. LSTM outperforms a basic RNN in accuracy and response time; the dataset is not described.

I299.summary_en: Develops three machine learning models, including a multi-tier approach, to identify elementary students needing mental health intervention using data from 2,600 students collected by the Healthier Kids Foundation and verified by clinicians. Models reach up to 94.5% accuracy across four mental health categories.

I300.screening_reason: Not about mental health; learning analytics review
I300.summary_en: Systematic review of 36 articles (2021-2025) on data-driven learning analytics and machine learning in higher education. Finds a disconnect between the models used and the available educational data and a lack of psychopedagogical and data governance frameworks.

I301.summary_en: Proposes a framework for predicting mental health issues from text using NLP and XGBoost, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression. No data or results are reported.

I302.summary_en: Trains machine learning models on facial action unit features extracted with OpenFace from 349 remote-learning videos of 76 college students to predict mental health states. Decision Tree performs best for depression (AUC 0.594), with AU09, AU25 and AU07 as the most important features.

I303.screening_reason: Main outcome is online academic performance
I303.summary_en: Examines factors affecting online academic performance using survey responses from 978 junior and senior high school students in the Philippines, Boruta feature selection, an MLP neural network and sensitivity analysis. The MLP reaches 0.932 accuracy, and motivation and mental well-being are the most sensitive factors.

I304.best_result: Bag of Words + Logistic Regression accuracy 77.78%, F1 0.79
I304.summary_en: Detects stress in posts from Reddit academic communities using NLP and classifiers trained on the Dreaddit dataset, validated on 100 manually annotated academic posts (72% accuracy). The overall stress level in academic texts is 29%, with professors' communities more stressed than bachelor's, graduate and PhD student communities.

I305.screening_reason: Focus on academic performance; conceptual review
I305.summary_en: Reviews how machine learning could extend cognitive behavioral therapy to address adolescents' academic challenges through personalized interventions. No included studies, data or results are reported.

I306.screening_reason: Outcome is academic outcomes; well-being only mentioned
I306.summary_en: Presents a hybrid framework combining machine learning classifiers and rough set rules to identify at-risk students from academic, behavioral and engagement data in the OULAD dataset. It reaches 97.85% accuracy, about 15% above conventional methods.

I307.summary_en: Identifies factors of mental health problems in 635 Malaysian university students by relating DASS-21 scores to WHOQOL facets with Two-step and k-means clustering. Students with severe scores rate lowest on study, self-esteem, memory and positive feelings.

I308.screening_reason: Population: homeless children, not framed as students
I308.summary_en: Develops an SVM model that screens the mental health status of homeless children from Pediatric Symptom Checklist responses for use by orphanage caretakers. The model achieves 90% accuracy.

I309.summary_en: Proposes a peer support application with a predictive tool that classifies speech emotion states of university students using convolutional neural networks to monitor mental health progress. No data or results are reported.

I310.summary_en: Proposes a system that detects student depression from facial expressions (CNN) and voice patterns, trained on a collected student face and audio dataset. It reports high accuracy without quantifying it.

I311.summary_en: Proposes an IoT and cloud system using wearables (heart rate, sleep, activity, stress) to track students' emotional and physical health in classrooms and link it to academic achievement with machine learning. No data or results are reported.

I312.summary_en: Designs a dynamic mental health early warning algorithm based on improved XGBoost with multi-source data fusion, tested on psychological, behavioral and academic data from 12,785 college students. It achieves 86% accuracy and AUC 0.91, outperforming SVM and RNN, with a two-week warning lead time.

I313.summary_en: Scoping review of eight articles on how AI has been used to improve mental health literacy in the United States. AI is used through role-play simulations, chatbots and LLMs, and machine and deep learning, mainly for depression, suicide prevention, ADHD and PTSD.

I314.summary_en: Proposes a multimodal framework for detecting depressive symptoms in university students and staff that fuses surveys, video interviews and social media text with NLP, computer vision, and deep and traditional machine learning. Strong predictive performance is claimed without metrics.

I315.summary_en: Proposes a Pelican-optimized feed-forward network to classify students' anxiety levels using Kaggle anxiety datasets, compared with other machine learning models. It reaches 0.983 accuracy and 0.982 F1 with 50% shorter model building time.

I316.summary_en: Proposes a machine learning system that analyzes psychological and academic data to identify students at mental health risk. No algorithms, data details or results are reported.

I317.screening_reason: Not about mental health; school dropout
I317.summary_en: Develops a platform that predicts school dropout risk in Colombia from national and local historical data using decision trees, SVM and neural networks, with a policy simulation module. The neural network achieves over 85% accuracy.

I318.screening_reason: Not about mental health; computing cluster for physical exercise
I318.summary_en: Studies load balancing in computing clusters and an AI training model applied to college students' physical exercise. Results are reported only as efficient.

I319.summary_en: Compares five models (Logistic Regression, KNN, Random Forest, Decision Tree, CNN) to predict depression in 927 Bangladeshi undergraduates assessed with a Bangla DASS-21. CNN achieves the highest accuracy (91%), followed by Random Forest (85%).

I320.screening_reason: Vague abstract; population includes various groups
I320.summary_en: Presents a Python-based data analysis of factors affecting mental health, targeting groups such as college students. Data, models and results are not described.

I321.summary_en: Proposes a multimodal Transformer model fusing BERT text vectors and ViT image vectors through tensor products to classify students' psychological conditions. It reaches 93.65% accuracy, outperforming CLIP and ViLBERT; the dataset is not described.

I322.summary_en: Predicts students' mental health status in online learning from survey responses using numerous classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, KNN, gradient boosting, MLP, stacking, among others). Decision Tree performs best (75% accuracy, F-score 82.7%).

I323.screening_reason: Outcome is motivation and engagement, not mental health; conceptual
I323.summary_en: Discusses how machine learning and NLP can predict and enhance student motivation and engagement from demographic, behavioral and textual data. No data or results are reported.

I324.screening_reason: Not about students; traumatic brain injury neuroimaging
I324.summary_en: Shows that harmonization of multi-site resting-state functional connectivity data should be integrated into machine learning classification of mild traumatic brain injury. No metrics are reported.

I325.summary_en: Analyzes the impact of social media on mental health using a dataset of 481 records with correlation analysis, visualization and several models. Gaussian Naive Bayes yields the highest accuracy, and social media engagement is associated with negative mental well-being.

I326.summary_en: Proposes a mental well-being chatbot for students using NLP, sentiment analysis and keyword detection, with Spotify mood-based music recommendations and Twilio distress alerts. No data or metrics are reported.

I327.screening_reason: Abstract discusses only ethical concerns; no data or method
I327.summary_en: Discusses privacy, discrimination and accuracy concerns of using machine learning for facial emotion recognition in students. No data, method or results are presented.

I328.summary_en: Detects loneliness in college students using smartphone passive sensing data from 41 students, unsupervised clustering into behavioral subgroups and group-specific classification models. Group-based models significantly improve accuracy over generalized models.

I329.summary_en: Predicts student stress levels from a Google Forms survey using the PSS-10 and SVM, KNN and Naive Bayes classifiers. SVM achieves the highest accuracy (95.32%).

I330.summary_en: Compares Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, SVM and Random Forest for predicting anxiety, depression and stress levels of undergraduate students from questionnaire scores. No sample size or metrics are reported.

I331.summary_en: Predicts anxiety in university students in Bangladesh from a Google Form survey using a voting classifier built on the three best algorithms and 20 selected features, explained with LIME and SHAP. The voting classifier reaches 96% accuracy.

I332.screening_reason: Not about mental health; digital literacy
I332.summary_en: Examines factors contributing to digital literacy and technology use among higher education students through semi-structured interviews and correlation analysis. No specific results are reported.

I333.summary_en: Compares six machine learning models to classify depression, anxiety and stress from DASS-21 profiles using 2,602 records from the University of Phayao Counselling Center. The deep learning model performs best, with accuracy above 90% and AUC above 99%.

I334.summary_en: Proposes machine learning models to predict suicide risk levels (high, medium, low) in college students from data such as depression levels and discrimination experiences. No data or results are reported.

I335.summary_en: Proposes CASTLE, a framework that fuses social life, academic performance and physical appearance data via representation learning (MOON network embedding), SMOTE and a deep neural network to detect university students' mental health problems. It reports promising performance against baselines without metrics.

I336.summary_en: Examines the influence of routine regularity and sleep quality on mental well-being in 376 participants using machine learning classification. XGBoost achieves 88.20% accuracy, and routine regularity and 7-9 hours of sleep are the strongest predictors.

I337.summary_en: Proposes a transformer-based sentiment analysis framework for student mental health monitoring from user-generated text. Multilingual BERT performs best; the dataset and metrics are not described.

I338.screening_reason: Psychological status is only one dimension of student portraits for class management
I338.summary_en: Proposes multi-dimensional student group portraits (academic performance, self-regulated learning, psychological status, social interaction) built with machine learning and a visualization system to assist university counselors in class meetings. No data or quantitative results are reported.

I339.summary_en: Predicts college students' mental stress around examinations and internet use from surveys at several institutions using Decision Tree, SVM, Naive Bayes and KNN. KNN achieves the highest accuracy (87.2%).

I340.screening_reason: Conceptual essay focused on personalized learning
I340.summary_en: Discusses how machine learning-based personalized learning and formative assessment could reduce closed-book examination stress. No data, method or results are presented.

I341.screening_reason: Does not address students; conceptual overview
I341.summary_en: Reviews AI types that may support mental health education and describes an AI-based chatbot platform for identifying mental health factors. No data or results are reported.

I342.summary_en: Trains machine learning models to estimate heart rate variability from heart rate and step count using 201 hours of wearable data from 14 university students. Highest-stress periods are predicted with moderate performance (AUC 0.746).

I343.summary_en: Screens mental disorders (mood, anxiety, depression, eating and sleep disorders) in students with supervised machine learning on SRQ-15 and SRQ-25 questionnaires. Algorithms and results are not reported.

I344.summary_en: Predicts nomophobia severity in 841 university students in Kosovo using Random Forest, descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation. Random Forest explains about 98% of the variance (R² 0.9773), and nomophobia correlates positively with anxiety, stress and depression.

I345.summary_en: Proposes a smart learning system that combines automatic question generation (T5, BERT) with a facial emotion recognition module to monitor student stress in online learning. No data or results are reported.

I346.best_result: Random Forest + Naive Bayes ensemble accuracy 99.57%
I346.summary_en: Assesses ensemble machine learning for detecting stress in 501 thesis students from seven universities using a modified Student-Life Stress Inventory. The Random Forest and Naive Bayes ensemble reaches 99.57% accuracy, surpassing individual baselines.

I347.screening_reason: Not about mental health; academic grades
I347.summary_en: Clusters and predicts student grades using a UCI open dataset to identify factors related to academic performance. No metrics are reported.

I348.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical health
I348.summary_en: Builds a big data platform for monitoring adolescents' physical health with machine learning on 15 fitness indicators, piloted in five schools with over 15,000 students. Early warning accuracy reaches 92.3%.

I349.summary_en: Predicts psychiatric diagnoses among undergraduates from demographic, lifestyle and psychometric survey data using various classifiers. The Multi-layer Perceptron is the most effective; sample size and metrics are not reported.

I350.summary_en: Proposes a system using CNN, LSTM and RNN to detect early-stage depression in students from standardized questionnaires and behavioral factors (mood, sleep, social interaction, school performance). No data size or results are reported.

I351.screening_reason: Not about mental health; bibliometric analysis of AI in learning
I351.summary_en: Bibliometric analysis of 185 Scopus publications on AI applications for international students' learning. Research output is growing and four thematic clusters are identified.
